key_findings: Independently reproduced both focal ANCOVAs exactly: Study 1 Numeracy F(1,393)=16.58 and Condition F(3,393)=49.46; Study 2 Numeracy F(1,395)=17.78 and Condition F(3,395)=19.18 — all match the paper and the human reproduction report.

Practical-significance-bias claim confirmed in both studies: the no-effect-size group endorsed more than the small-effect-no-prompt group (Study 1 marginal diff 34.89, p<.0001; Study 2 14.76, p=.002) while not differing from the large-effect group (Study 1 +6.07 ns; Study 2 -7.54 ns).
Interaction F-values reproduced (Study 1 F(3,390)=3.69, p=.012; Study 2 F(3,392)=3.13, p=.026) matching the paper and report.
Study 2 per-condition numeracy correlations reproduced (SmallEffNoPrompt r=-.19; SmallEffWithPrompt r=-.42; both ~<.1 otherwise).

Descriptive means reproduced; Study 2 means exactly match (50.47/58.90/34.98/31.68), Study 1 small-group means differ slightly from the printed text (45.18 vs 45.26; 45.02 vs 45.22) as the human report also noted.

Reproduction infrastructure issues: the FLoRA node s4et7 ships only the report PDF + R script with a hardcoded local path (D:/Meta_Rep_Games/) and NO data/analysis-code file; raw data had to be pulled from the authors' project osf.io/4927f. No cleaning/analysis code was provided by authors.
notes: Actual paper title is 'A Practical Significance Bias in Laypeople's Evaluation of Scientific Findings' (Michal & Shah, 2024, Psych. Science 35(4):315-327); DOI 10.1177/09567976241231506 resolves to this, not the 'Heuristic for Inference and Prediction' title given in the task. OSF hint s4et7 is the correct FLoRA reproduction. Focal tests verified exactly, consistent with the human FLoRA report (Röer, Ostermann & Appelbaum) which judged the reproduction 'largely successful' with only minor-to-moderate reporting errors. The registry 'flora=computational issues' reflects analytic/reporting obstacles (missing mean-difference method, missing CI signs, n2/eta discrepancies, text mean typos, a double preregistration for Study 1), not a failure to reproduce headline results.
